gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=3

## Main case: re-entry with a retained `deliver` course at both caps

**Tracker.** The original init held `gather, provision, verify`. There was no `--rebase`, so there is no `sync` stage. On this re-entry I `add` `report` and then `menu` only when each starts. The first tracker task name carries `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`.

**Commands, in order**

1. **Validate the run record.**
   - I read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`.
   - `consent.target` is `{ acme/widgets, 42, main }`, which matches the lowercase base repository, the PR number and `baseRefName`.
   - The record shows course `deliver`, `rounds_used 10 / rounds_cap 10`, `syncs_used 10 / syncs_cap 10`, `wave: null` and `poll_deadline: null`.
   - It is readable, so I reset nothing.
2. **Exit check, ordered.** There is no retained helper `open - needs` result and no no-progress checkpoint.
   - **Readiness fails** because P1 is open and the forge reports `BEHIND`.
   - **Obstacle table:** the only applicable row is CONFLICTING/BEHIND plus a repairable gap. That row continues the D3 body only while accounting permits.
   - **Cap row matches:** rounds_used has reached rounds_cap, giving `round cap reached: 10 of 10`. The sync cap is also exhausted at `10 of 10`.
   - I render the obstacle template and keep the local state as is. There is no Loop sync and no wave.
3. **Pre-menu refresh (read-only).**
   - `gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
   - `gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
   - The results are an unchanged head and an unchanged body ("Reject unsigned events."). `baseRefName` is `main`, which equals `consent.target`. The state is OPEN, mergeable is MERGEABLE, and `mergeStateStatus` is `BEHIND`.
   - Check `ci / test` and run 910 are SUCCESS, so there are no pending checks.
4. **Re-entry point.** The head is unchanged, so this re-enters step 5. No helper is dispatched.
5. **Evidence and assessed SHA.** Verification evidence and the brief both assess `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.
   - The evidence source is `ci` (run 910, `ci / test` success).
   - Comments are empty, so there are no `C#` rows and no replies.

**Sync line:** none renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

**Rendered report and menu**

```text
Delivers: the event guard rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. An unsigned event wrapped in an array still passes the guard, so the bypass the PR sets out to close stays open. (src/guard.mjs; src/guard.test.mjs)

Round cap reached: 10 of 10; sync cap reached: 10 of 10. The branch is also behind main, which needs one more sync. Local commits are kept.

Evidence: CI (run 910, ci / test green on 1111111)
Verdict: not ready - round cap reached: 10 of 10

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; repair the array bypass and sync onto main, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (+2 x 5: rounds 10/10 -> 10/20, syncs 10/10 -> 10/20).
2. assess - switch course: post the open blocker as one comment review, no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (round cap reached; merge_state_status BEHIND)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI run 910, ci / test green on 1111111).
```

**Human reply: `1`.**
- `1` is in range 1-3 and no list precedes the options, so it maps unchanged to `deliver`.
- I persist the following before any work: `rounds_cap 20`, `syncs_cap 20`, `rounds_used 10`, `syncs_used 10` (usage unchanged), course `deliver`, `poll_deadline` still null.
- The narration stops here, before any new helper result.

**Accounting**

| History item | Rounds | Syncs |
|---|---|---|
| Ten reviewed source-changing waves | 10 (one each, charged once when a dispatched payload left a new source-changing commit) | - |
| Mixed source-changing wave that also synced | one round, already among the 10 | one sync |
| Conflict-only syncs | 0 | one each |
| Loop syncs, conflict-only ones included | - | 10 in total |
| Description-only writes, watches, re-reviews | 0 | 0 |

The extension adds exactly `2 x maxFixRounds` (5, the resolved override) to each cap and never resets usage. Usage is therefore 10/20 rounds and 10/20 syncs. The verify-phase `closureReview` guard (`1 x maxFixRounds`) is untouched.

## Independent B: the runtime guard refuses the dispatch

- After the extension, the Exit check passes on accounting (10 < 20 for both).
- The D3 body runs Loop sync first, because the forge is BEHIND. Same-author and no merge commits means the rebase path, with no conflict assumed. It records `repair.wave.sync` and increments `syncs_used` to 11 before the sync.
- In the actual order, the wave dispatch comes first: the step-1 fix wave attempts one fresh `implementer` with `cwd /work/widgets-pr-42`. Its task carries:
  - P1's evidence pack;
  - the stored scope baseline;
  - `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: node --test src/guard.test.mjs`;
  - the commit-only-on-green rule, otherwise discard and return `open - <why>`;
  - the before/after report shape.
- The runtime refuses that dispatch before any work.
- No commit lands and no round is charged, so usage stays at 10 rounds. The guard owns the result: `stuck - phase-tracker fix-round guard: closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached`.
- I render the obstacle with that verdict verbatim and do not bypass it. Rows: `deliver` (resume; +10 each cap, 10/20 -> 10/30) / `assess` / `stop [recommended]`.

## Independent C: unchanged no-progress checkpoint

- I validate the record, then evaluate `repair.wave.no_progress` before any course work or watch.
- The failed input is unchanged: the same test, the same source and inputs, the same command, and the result at `/tmp/guard-failed.synthetic` is still red.
- The exit is `stuck - no progress: node --test src/guard.test.mjs: constant-time comparison`. I dispatch no helper and push nothing.
- Usage stays 10/20 and 10/20. The higher cap is not permission to repeat the attempt.
- Obstacle rows: `deliver` (retry after the constant-time comparison input changes, no round charged; +10 each cap) / `assess` / `stop [recommended]`.

## Independent D: held workflow run the viewer cannot approve

**Obstacle report and menu**

```text
Delivers: the event guard rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. An unsigned event wrapped in an array still passes the guard, so the bypass the PR sets out to close stays open. (src/guard.mjs; src/guard.test.mjs)

The workflow run on the assessed head is awaiting approval, which this viewer cannot grant.

Evidence: pending (held workflow run binding; head 1111111)
Verdict: not ready - stuck - workflow run awaiting approval

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retry once the held run is approved, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (+2 x 5: rounds 2/10 -> 2/20, syncs 1/10 -> 1/20).
2. assess - switch course: post the open blocker as one comment review, no repairs.
3. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Not offered: approve workflow run (viewer cannot approve the held run); merge (workflow run awaiting approval)
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (held run pending on 1111111).
```

**Human clears the held run externally and replies `1`.**
- The reply maps unchanged to `deliver`.
- I persist the following before any work: `rounds_cap 20`, `syncs_cap 20`, `rounds_used 2`, `syncs_used 1`, course `deliver`.
- The narration stops before another helper result.

gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=3

This is a hypothetical narration; no tools run. A-D are independent continuations, not consecutive extensions of one record.

## Shared entry state

I retain `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` and validate its immutable target as `acme/widgets`, PR 42, base `main`. I do not initialize another record, reset accounting, or rerun provisioning.

The original invocation initializes tracker stages `gather`, `provision`, and `verify`, with `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` in the first task's name. It has no `sync` stage because the arguments are `42`, without `--rebase`. At this retained-course entry, I reopen or add `report` and then `menu` only as each starts.

Verification and the brief remain bound to `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. No new Verify or whole-diff Review helper is dispatched merely to render these retained-state menus. No `Sync:` line renders in any case; loop sync history does not create an entry-sync report line.

For each report below, I perform the pre-menu refresh with these commands, in order:

```sh
gh pr view 42 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
```

The retained body, base, and head match. Each independent entry supplies its own retained obstacle and evidence state.

## A. Both course caps reached

The refresh retains `BEHIND`. The unsigned-array bypass remains open. Exit check reaches the round cap before the sync-cap row, so the concrete exit is `round cap reached: 10 of 10`; both counters remain visible in the report.

No repair, fetch, sync, watch, push, or helper dispatch runs before the menu.

### First rendered menu

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=3

Delivers: The PR intends to reject unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. Unsigned array events bypass rejection, so the promised guard remains incomplete.

The round cap is reached at 10 of 10. Sync usage is also 10 of 10, and the branch remains behind main.

Evidence: CI (source: ci; run 910, ci / test success on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; binding-pending count 0; merge_state_status BEHIND)
Verdict: not ready - round cap reached: 10 of 10

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retry the unsigned-array repair and required base sync, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (rounds 10/10 -> 10/20, syncs 10/10 -> 10/20).
2. assess - post the open blocker to the PR without repairs.
3. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (unsigned-array rejection remains incomplete and the branch is behind main).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI, run 910, ci / test success on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111).
```

The human selects **1**, the displayed `deliver` row. I validate the existing record and persist, before work:

```text
course: deliver
repair.rounds_used: 10
repair.rounds_cap: 20
repair.syncs_used: 10
repair.syncs_cap: 20
```

The increment is exactly `2 x 5 = 10` to each cap. The selection itself charges neither counter. I stop narration here, before any new helper result.

The historical accounting remains cumulative:

- Ten source-changing repair passes account for ten rounds.
- Ten loop syncs account for ten syncs, including conflict-only syncs.
- Description-only writes consume no rounds.
- A source-changing wave that also syncs consumes one round and one sync.
- Restored failures, empty waves, reviews, and watches consume no rounds.
- Extending these course caps does not reset or extend the separate runtime fix-round guard.

## B. Runtime refuses the next dispatch

This case starts independently at caps `20/20` and usage `10/10`. Course accounting permits another attempt, but it does not override `closureReview.enforce`.

If the next repair dispatch is reached, I validate the record, retain the existing payload and scope baseline, and perform the wave's pre-work commands:

```sh
git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 rev-parse HEAD
git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 fetch origin main
git -C /work/widgets-pr-42 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-implementer.XXXXXX"
```

I persist the pass checkpoint before requesting the helper.

The requested dispatch is a fresh, synchronous `implementer` with cwd `/work/widgets-pr-42`. Its task carries:

- The recorded unsigned-array blocker payload and original PR-owned scope.
- A requirement to confirm the expected HEAD before work.
- The scoped command `node --test src/guard.test.mjs`, with failing-before and passing-after results.
- The smallest scope-preserving repair, without new infrastructure, dependencies, or modules.
- One commit only after the scoped test passes; otherwise restoration of its own edits and an `open` result.
- An `open - contract exception` return instead of changing the promised contract.
- The supplied temporary output path and the implementer output contract.

The runtime refuses the request:

```text
closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached
```

No helper executes. No source-changing commit exists, so usage remains `10/10`, with caps `20/20`. I do not change personas, bypass the guard, or treat the larger course caps as runtime permission.

After the two pre-menu refresh commands listed above, the first menu is:

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=3

Delivers: The PR intends to reject unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. Unsigned array events bypass rejection, so the promised guard remains incomplete.

The runtime refused the repair dispatch with "closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached". Usage remains rounds 10/20 and syncs 10/20.

Evidence: CI (source: ci; run 910, ci / test success on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111)
Verdict: not ready - stuck - phase-tracker fix-round guard: closureReview.enforce: maximum fix rounds reached

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retry dispatch only after the runtime prerequisite changes, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (rounds 10/20 -> 10/30, syncs 10/20 -> 10/30).
2. assess - post the open blocker to the PR without repairs.
3. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (unsigned-array rejection remains incomplete).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI, run 910, ci / test success on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111).
```

An unchanged runtime prerequisite re-exits even if another cap extension is selected.

## C. Retained no-progress checkpoint

This case independently starts at usage `10/10`, caps `20/20`.

Immediately after validating the record, I inspect the retained checkpoint. The failed prerequisite remains:

```text
node --test src/guard.test.mjs: constant-time comparison
```

Its source, input, and command are unchanged. The prior helper restored its edits and made no commit. I retain `/tmp/guard-failed.synthetic` as the result path.

I dispatch no helper, rerun no test, and start no CI watch. The checkpoint takes precedence over available course capacity. After the two pre-menu refresh commands, I render:

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=3

Delivers: The PR intends to reject unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. The constant-time comparison test remains red after the attempted repair was restored, so that repair has no passing scoped evidence. (src/guard.test.mjs: constant-time comparison)

The failed test's source, input, and command are unchanged. Usage remains rounds 10/20 and syncs 10/20.

Evidence: CI (source: ci; run 910, ci / test success on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111); the retained scoped repair attempt failed.
Verdict: not ready - stuck - no progress: node --test src/guard.test.mjs: constant-time comparison

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retry the repair only after its failed prerequisite changes, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (rounds 10/20 -> 10/30, syncs 10/20 -> 10/30).
2. assess - post the open blocker to the PR without repairs.
3. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: merge (the repair remains unresolved).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (CI, run 910, ci / test success on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111; retained failed scoped attempt).
```

The restored attempt adds no round. More capacity does not authorize repeating the unchanged failed attempt.

## D. Held workflow prerequisite

This independent case restores course `deliver`, rounds `2/10`, and syncs `1/10`. The retained obstacle is workflow approval unavailable to this viewer.

After validating the record and running the two pre-menu refresh commands, I retain the held-run evidence as `source: pending`. I dispatch no helper and run no approval API call or watch before the menu.

### First rendered menu

```text
gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/obstacle recommended=3

Delivers: The PR intends to reject unsigned events.

PR comments:
- The held workflow run awaits approval that this viewer cannot provide, so merge waits.

Usage remains rounds 2/10 and syncs 1/10.

Evidence: pending (held workflow run binding; head 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111)
Verdict: not ready - stuck - workflow run awaiting approval

Pick one:
1. deliver - resume the retained course; retry after the held-run prerequisite changes, no round charged; add 10 to each cap (rounds 2/10 -> 2/20, syncs 1/10 -> 1/20).
2. assess - post any open blockers to the PR without repairs.
3. stop - remove the eligible gate worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: approve workflow run (this viewer cannot approve the held run).
Not offered: merge (workflow run awaiting approval).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record (pending, held workflow run binding on 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111).
```

The human clears the held-run prerequisite externally and selects **1**.

I validate the record and persist the selection before work:

```text
course: deliver
repair.rounds_used: 2
repair.rounds_cap: 20
repair.syncs_used: 1
repair.syncs_cap: 20
```

I then run the same `gh pr view` and exact-head `gh run list` refresh commands to reconcile the externally changed prerequisite. Approval being cleared does not itself establish a successful run.

The extension is cumulative, adds exactly ten to each cap, and leaves usage at `2/1`. It neither resets accounting nor grants runtime-guard permission. I stop before another helper result.
